exact_wording: 2.—(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, a person who is not a party to a contract (called in this Act a third party) may, in the third party's own right, enforce a term of the contract if (a) the contract expressly provides that the third party may; or (b) subject to subsection (2), the term purports to confer a benefit on the third party. (2) Subsection (1)(b) does not apply if, on a proper construction of the contract, it appears that the parties did not intend the term to be enforceable by the third party. (3) The third party must be expressly identified in the contract by name, as a member of a class or as answering a particular description, but need not be in existence when the contract is entered into. (4) This section does not confer a right on a third party to enforce a term of a contract otherwise than subject to and in accordance with any other relevant terms of the contract.
summary: A non-party may enforce a contract term if the contract expressly says so, or if the term purports to confer a benefit on them (unless the parties evidently did not intend enforceability), provided the third party is identified by name, class or description.
applicability_conditions: contract entered into on or after 1 January 2002 (or entered into earlier but expressly provides for the application of this Act)
no express clause found excluding or disclaiming CRTPA / third-party rights

contract type is not one to which the s.7 exceptions remove third-party enforcement entirely (e.g. contracts of employment as against the employee, negotiable instruments, company constitution documents, certain carriage contracts)

exact_wording: (6) Where a term of a contract excludes or limits liability in relation to any matter, references in this Act to the third party enforcing the term are to be construed as references to the third party availing himself, herself or itself of the exclusion or limitation.

exact_wording: 7.—(1) Section 2 does not confer any right on a third party in the case of a contract on a bill of exchange, promissory note or other negotiable instrument. (2) Section 2 does not confer any right on a third party in the case of any contract binding on a company and its members under section 39 of the Companies Act 1967. (4) Section 2 does not confer any right on a third party to enforce any term of a contract of employment against an employee. (5) Section 2 does not confer any right on a third party in the case of (a) a contract for the carriage of goods by sea; or (b) a contract for the carriage of goods by rail or road, or for the carriage of cargo by air, which is subject to the rules of the appropriate international transport convention, except that a third party may in reliance on that section avail the third party of an exclusion or limitation of liability in such a contract.
summary: CRTPA third-party enforcement rights do not arise at all for negotiable instruments, a company's constitutional documents, contracts of employment as against the employee, or (subject to an exclusion/limitation-availment carve-out) carriage-of-goods contracts by sea, rail, road or air.
applicability_conditions: contract classified as employment, or otherwise falls within one of the s.7 categories (negotiable instrument, company constitutional document, or carriage of goods by sea/rail/road/air)

exact_wording: (2) Section 2(2) of the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 (exclusion of or restriction on liability for negligence) does not apply where the negligence consists of the breach of an obligation arising from a term of a contract and the person seeking to enforce it is a third party acting in reliance on section 2.
summary: UCTA's s.2(2) reasonableness requirement for negligence-liability exclusions is disapplied where the negligence is a breach of a contractual term and the person relying on it is a third party enforcing under CRTPA s.2 — relevant cross-check before firing the UCTA s.2(2) validator on a clause a third party might invoke.
